name: risk_management.json
description: Position sizing, loss control, drawdown protocols and survival-first risk rules. Rules are educational defaults, not personalized advice.
principle: Survival first. Risk management determines whether any edge can compound; entries matter less than sizing and loss control.

rules: Learning phase: 0.25% to 0.5% of equity per trade.
Proven phase: 0.5% to 1%. Hard cap 2% (Deriv educational guidance mentions 1-2%).
High-volatility indices (V100, V150, V250, Boom/Crash, Jump): use the lower end.
Size comes from stop distance: units = (equity * risk%) / stop_distance. Never choose size first.

rules.value: 2% to 3% (up to 5% for looser plans); stop trading for the day when hit.
6% to 10%; reduce size by half next week if hit.
After 2 to 3 losses in a row, pause or end the session.
At 10% drawdown from peak, go back to demo or half size and review the journal.
Set a number (e.g. 3 to 5) in advance.

methods.name: Structure stop
methods.how: Beyond the swing high/low that invalidates the idea, plus a buffer.

methods.name: ATR stop
methods.how: Entry -/+ k*ATR(14). Typical k: 1.0 (low vol), 1.2 (mid), 1.5 (high), 1.8-2.0 (very high).

methods.name: Time stop
methods.how: Exit if the trade has not worked after N bars or after the expected regime duration.

methods.name: Spread-based stop (pairs)
methods.how: Exit if z-score of spread exceeds e.g. 3 or 3.5 in the wrong direction.

rules: Always set the stop at entry.
Only ever move a stop in the direction that reduces risk.
Never widen a stop after entry.

methods: Next structure level or measured move.
Partial profit: close 50% at 1R, move stop to breakeven, trail remainder.
Trail behind EMA20 or swing points or Chandelier stop.
Time-based exit before expected regime end (Drift Switch).
topics.caution: Breakeven stops can reduce win rate; test whether partials and breakeven help or hurt expectancy.

topics.text: A strategy needs positive expectancy AFTER costs. Expectancy_R = win_rate*avgWinR - (1-win_rate)*avgLossR. Example: 40% win rate, avg win 2R, avg loss 1R -> 0.4*2 - 0.6*1 = +0.2R per trade. Same win rate with 1.2R average win -> 0.48 - 0.6 = -0.12R (losing).

topics.formula: Kelly fraction f* = W - (1-W)/R, where W = win probability, R = avg win / avg loss.
topics.guidance: Full Kelly is too aggressive and very sensitive to estimation error. Use at most 1/4 to 1/2 Kelly, and cap risk at 1-2% anyway. If estimated edge is uncertain or negative, f* <= 0 means do not trade.

topics.text: Risk of ruin rises sharply with larger risk per trade and lower expectancy. With 1% risk and positive expectancy, ruin probability is tiny; with 10% risk it is high even with a decent edge.
topics.simulation_hint: Monte Carlo: resample trade R-results thousands of times, track max drawdown and ruin frequency for different risk-per-trade values.

topics.text: Probability of at least one losing streak of length L in 100 trades with a 50% win rate: L=5 about 81%; L=7 about 38%; L=10 about 9%. Streaks are normal; size so that a 10-loss streak is survivable (10 x 1% = about 9.6% drawdown).

rules: Highly correlated positions (correlation above about 0.7) count as ONE exposure for risk.
Total open risk cap: e.g. 3% to 5% of equity across all trades.
Several Deriv indices are independent random processes in theory, but several simultaneous high-volatility positions still multiply risk of simultaneous large losses; limit open positions.
Avoid being long and short highly correlated assets by accident (it cancels edge and doubles costs).
Leverage is not a risk setting; stop distance and risk% are.
Keep margin used well below available equity (e.g. under 20-30%).

On very high-volatility synthetics, small lot sizes are normal; minimum lot may force more risk than 1% on small accounts. If minimum lot risk exceeds your cap, do not trade that instrument or fund more.
Account for gaps/spikes: on Crash/Boom and Jump indices a stop can be skipped by a spike, so actual loss may exceed planned stop.

items: Swap/financing for overnight holds (Deriv example: DSI 10 annual swap around 7.5% in its KID; check current).
Rule: target distance should be at least 5-10x the spread, otherwise costs dominate.

list: Averaging down into a losing position without predefined risk.
Increasing size after losses to 'win it back'.
Trading without a plan or while emotional, tired or intoxicated.
Risking money needed for living expenses.
Using real money before demo and backtest validation.

research_context: The Kelly criterion maximizes long-run growth but full-Kelly sizing is highly volatile; practitioners commonly use fractional Kelly or fixed-fractional risk instead.
Fixed-fractional sizing risks a constant percentage of equity adjusted for stop distance; it is the standard retail baseline.
